doc.title: Pete Candoli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999

title: Overdubbing for Alabama and Chicago, and respect for all music
summary: Pete speaks of dubbing for rock groups and his philosophy of respecting all genres.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: And Chicago, yeah. We had many other groups, you know they liked the sound of something acoustic for a change of course, which was great. There are some good musicians, really marvelous players, but so much heavy garbage thrown in. It’s like jazz sometimes, you know, you can hear it all the time or blues, or what you call jazz, there’s the fine or good things you want to pick out, that are memorable, academically speaking, memorable, good interpretation for a jazz type of thing. And then there’s a lot of filler.
Yeah, a lot of filler. That’s a good usable word.

And God bless, everybody can do something. I don’t care what field you’re in, if it’s country western, be the best it can, that’s my kind of philosophy. I don’t put anything down like that. That’s it. And their taste, and what they like, is as valid as mine. I’m just another person. Hopefully they would respect me the same with my taste, I don’t know. But I’m talking so much really—
No, it’s amazing when you think that you could be riding down the street and be listening to something old or fairly new and you probably think, you know I think I played on that.
